title: Space frame of three members under joint loads

source.work: Bentley Systems, STAAD.Pro Help, Verification Examples (public documentation, docs.bentley.com)
source.edition: STAAD.Pro Help v21 build (pages refer to the STAAD.Pro 2023 sample files), read 2026-11-22
source.notes: problem statement taken from the vendor page (text and input listing). The page cites: Weaver, Computer Programs for Structural Analysis, p. 146, problem 8 - NOT opened for this project; no number is taken from it. The page's 'theory' values are recorded as printed; the program's own results are not used.

analysis: Space frame, global Y vertical: nodes 1 (0, 120, 0), 2 (240, 120, 0), 3 (0, 0, 0), 4 (360, 0, 120) in; members 1-2, 3-1, 2-4, all A = 11 in^2, torsion constant 83 in^4, Iy = Iz = 56 in^4; E = 30,000 ksi, nu = 0.25 (G = 12,000 ksi); nodes 3 and 4 built in. Loads: 2 kip along +X at node 1; 1 kip downward and a moment of 120 kip in about -Z at node 2. First-order analysis, no shear deformation. Of the page's three printed values only the largest axial force (member 2-4) is used: its largest bending moments 'about local y' and 'about local z' depend on the vendor's local-axis convention for an inclined member, which the page does not state. Reference values: computed here from this statement (verification/derive/vendor_reference.py); the textbook cited by the vendor page was not opened and no number is taken from it.
